implementation_notes: The platform ships structuredClone(), which deep-copies object graphs, preserves cycles and handles Map/Set/Date/ArrayBuffer - for plain configuration data this is exactly the prototype intent: clone a pre-configured object and tweak fields. It does not walk or duplicate the prototype chain, so class instances come back as plain objects and functions or DOM nodes throw DataCloneError. Use it for data-only graphs; for behaviour-carrying objects implement a clone() method.
pitfalls: structuredClone strips the prototype chain: clone instanceof Shape is false and prototype methods are gone, while the declared type may still claim otherwise.
Functions, DOM nodes, WeakMap/WeakSet and symbol values throw DataCloneError, so event handlers or closures in a prototype break the clone outright.
Property descriptors, getters/setters and non-enumerable properties are not preserved - only the current value is copied.

variants.name: hand-written clone() preserving the class prototype
variants.implementation_notes: When instances carry behaviour, cloning must keep the prototype: write a clone() method (or a copy constructor / static from() factory) that creates a new instance of the actual class and deep-copies the mutable own fields. This is the only JavaScript realization that produces true polymorphic clones of a class hierarchy - map over the shapes and let each clone itself - and it is also where the deep/shallow decision is made explicit per field.
pitfalls: A clone() that returns new Shape(...) instead of the concrete class slices the subclass: instanceof and overridden methods break.
Fields holding listeners, AbortControllers or timers are shared by the clone unless the method explicitly re-creates them.
Spread/Object.assign inside clone() is shallow: nested objects stay shared, so the clone is only independent at the top level.
